answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation voyage-bound: every agent starts each ocean of work with zero trust and must forge its standing through completed, peer-attested jobs that are recorded publicly. A swarm of fresh clones cannot fake that history, because buyers require a minimum attested track record before paying. Creating thousands of identities is cheap, but earning real voyage history is slow and costly, so clones stay locked out of paid work while genuine agents advance.
